- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.34), especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (<0.27) or trending downward, particularly in the middle-to-late forecast window.
- Avoid sharp upward forecasts when recent price action shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline).
- Reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative and price history shows downward momentum.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is significantly lower than forecast in the first 3–5 days, adjust subsequent days downward by 1–2% per day to reflect momentum decay.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast peaks >15% above recent 7-day average, reduce peak by 10–15% and flatten slope for next 3–5 days.
- Use sentiment as a volatility filter: if sentiment >0.4, allow 10–15% higher forecast variance; if <0.2, constrain variance to 5–8%.
